newsitem.title: UK: Canadian Pacific completes Lykes takeover.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific completes Lykes takeover.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd said Wednesday it had completed the acquisition of the container shipping operations of Lykes Bros. Steamship Co for $34 million.
The company said the U.S. firm's operations had now been registered with a new Tampa, Florida-based company, Lykes Lines Limited, which is part of the CP Ships group.
Former chief executive of Cast, which is also part of CP Ships, has been appointed chief executive officer of Lykes.
CP ships began the acquisition of Lykes Bros in December 1996 -- 15 months after the company had filed for protection under Chapter 11 of U.S. bankruptcy law.
The process was delayed by the Washington Maritime Administration's rejection of the continuation of operating subsidies for three U.S. flagged Lykes ships, worth a total $6.3 million.
The subsidies, which are granted for making the ships available in time of emergency, were withdrawn because it was felt the company was coming under "excessive foreign control."
The Marad ruling could have implications for the proposed $825 million merger between APL Ltd and Neptune Orient Lines Ltd which also involves U.S. subsidies.
Canadian Pacific said Lykes Lines will charter in six container ships and two conventional vessels formerly employed by Lykes Bros. The ships will remain U.S. owned, operated and flagged, it added.
